We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

We have guidance: steps forward: 1) carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse: Starting from target, break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So reverse: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). Then sulfonamide formation forward: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. Reverse: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and amine.

Thus we need three retrosynthetic steps: Step1: disconnection of amide (C=O-N) to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (the aniline attached to amide). Step2: disconnection of α,β-unsaturated acid to give aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl with sulfonyl group) and malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). Step3: disconnection of sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the aromatic amine attached to sulfonyl). The final precursors should be simple: maybe p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride, aniline, malonic acid, and an aromatic aldehyde (maybe p-tolyl aldehyde). Let's examine target: It has a tolyl (C) attached to phenyl ring with sulfonamide linking to another phenyl ring bearing the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain.

Structure: p-tolyl (C) attached to phenyl (ring1) with NSO2 attached to second phenyl (ring2). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to ring1 (tolyl phenyl). The sulfonyl group attached to ring2 which also has the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Target (mol) -> Reaction3 (sulfonamide formation) reverse: break NSO2 to give sulfonyl chloride attached to ring2 and amine (aniline) attached to ring1 (p-toluidine). So precursors: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and sulfonyl chloride (maybe 4-(...?) Actually sulfonyl chloride attached to ring2 which also has the unsaturated amide side chain. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is a phenyl sulfonyl chloride bearing the unsaturated amide side chain (i.e., 4-(α,β-unsaturated amide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride). That seems complex. But maybe we can break further: The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the same aromatic ring that later will have the unsaturated amide attached via a carbon chain. So we need to generate that aromatic sulfonyl chloride from the unsaturated acid precursor via step2? Actually step2 is Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to the aromatic ring (ring2). That unsaturated acid is attached to the aromatic ring via a carbonyl (C=O) after amide formation. Wait the unsaturated acid is part of the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid is the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to the aromatic ring via a double bond (aryl-CH=CH-COOH). In target, the COOH is converted to amide with aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring2 (the sulfonyl phenyl). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same aromatic ring with the unsaturated acid still as acid (not amide). So step2: unsaturated acid derived from aldehyde + malonic acid. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor after step2 is aromatic sulfonyl chloride bearing the unsaturated acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH). Then step1: amide formation attaches aniline to that acid.

Thus final precursors after three steps: 1) p-toluidine (aniline with methyl). 2) 4-(sulfonyl chloride) phenyl with unsaturated acid side chain (aryl-CH=CH-COOH). 3) malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). 4) aromatic aldehyde (the same phenyl ring without side chain? Actually the aldehyde is the aromatic aldehyde that after Doebner gives the unsaturated acid attached to same aromatic ring. So the aldehyde is the phenyl sulfonyl chloride bearing an aldehyde group (aryl-CHO). So we need to propose that as a precursor.

Thus route: Step A (retro amide): target -> unsaturated acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N). The unsaturated acid is attached to sulfonyl phenyl. So we need to represent that as a molecule SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 attached to SO2? Actually the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to sulfonyl group linking to the other phenyl (p-tolyl). So the unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl phenyl: The sulfonyl phenyl is the one bearing the unsaturated acid. Its SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2S(=O)(=O)?? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the other phenyl via N. In the target, NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to N. In the unsaturated acid precursor after breaking amide, we have the same sulfonyl phenyl attached to N? Actually after breaking amide, we have the sulfonyl phenyl attached to N (still sulfonamide). Wait the amide is attached to the unsaturated acid carbonyl, not to the sulfonyl phenyl. The amide nitrogen is attached to the unsaturated acid carbonyl (C(=O)N...). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl and to the p-tolyl phenyl. So after breaking amide, we still have sulfonamide intact. So step1 only breaks amide, leaving sulfonamide unchanged. So the unsaturated acid precursor still has sulfonamide linking the two phenyl rings. So the unsaturated acid precursor SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1. That's the same as target but with COOH instead of CONH-aryl. So we need that as a precursor.

Step2 (retro Doebner): break unsaturated acid to give aromatic aldehyde (same phenyl sulfonyl) with CHO and malonic acid. The aldehyde precursor SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 (i.e., aromatic aldehyde attached to sulfonyl phenyl). And malonic acid: HOOC-CH2-COOH.

Step3 (retro sulfonamide formation): break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic aldehyde (same as above but with SO2Cl) and p-toluidine (aniline with methyl). So sulfonyl chloride precursor SMILES: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl that also has the aldehyde? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl that also has the aldehyde (the sulfonyl phenyl). So its SMILES: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? But also need the aldehyde substituent on same ring: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 with aldehyde at para? The original sulfonyl phenyl has the aldehyde at para relative to sulfonyl? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl has the unsaturated side chain at para to the sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The sulfonyl phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) has the side chain at para position relative to the sulfonyl? The SMILES shows c2ccc( side )cc2, with sulfonyl attached to N (NSO2). The side chain is at position 4 relative to sulfonyl? Not sure but we can assume same position.

Thus sulfonyl chloride precursor SMILES: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 with aldehyde at para? Actually we need both substituents: the aldehyde side chain is attached to the same phenyl ring as sulfonyl chloride. So SMILES: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 with an aldehyde at para? That would be Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? No aldehyde missing. Should be something like: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 with an aldehyde substituent maybe at position 4 relative to sulfonyl. Could be Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1C=O? Actually need to place aldehyde on same ring: maybe "Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1C=O". But need correct SMILES: "Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1C=O". That is a tolyl ring with sulfonyl chloride and aldehyde substituents.

But the aldehyde is attached to the same phenyl as sulfonyl chloride, not the tolyl phenyl. The tolyl phenyl is the other phenyl (the one attached to N). So the sulfonyl phenyl is not methyl-substituted. Actually the methyl is on the first phenyl (p-tolyl) attached to N. The sulfonyl phenyl does not have methyl. So the aldehyde precursor SMILES: c1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1C=O (no methyl). The p-toluidine is "Cc1ccc(N)cc1". Good.

Thus final route:

Target (mol) -> Reaction1 (amide formation) reverse: children: unsaturated acid (mol) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Reaction template id for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). We'll need template ID; we can search for amide formation template. Use search with functional_groups_broken: "C-O" maybe? But we can approximate using generic template ID? We need actual ID from database. Let's search for amide formation template.
